A tax audit doesn't even mean that you've, necessarily, done anything wrong. It is simply one of the processes by which the IRS reviews your tax returns, potentially with requesting additional information.

A huge number of things can make it more likely that your return will be audited, such as excessive deductions, suspicious charitable donations, not reporting income, etc. But at the time of the audit, there is not even a finding of wrongdoing.

Even if the IRS, for example, disallows some deductions and claims that your owe more taxes, it will basically result in a tax bill, probably with fines and interest.

To be a felon, you have to be tried and convicted in a criminal court. For that, you have to commit Tax Evasion. In a very extreme case, a tax audit could lead to a criminal prosecution of tax evasion, but that isn't common in any normal course of events.

So, no, a tax audit does not make you a felon.
